Get EUNIS habitat types

Markus Bauer, Mariasole Calbi & Gilles Colling

Source: vignettes/EUNIS.Rmd
EUNIS.Rmd

This vignette shows how to classify European vegetation relevés into EUNIS habitat types using the expert system of Chytrý et al. (2020). Habitat descriptions are available on FloraVeg.EU (Chytrý et al. 2024) and the EEA EUNIS website.

First, resy_harmonize_eunis() prepares the plot data. It adds geographic information such as country, ecoregion and coastal position, and checks and adjusts the coordinate format and species names to meet the expert system’s requirements. Then, resy_classify() assigns the relevés to habitat types using their species composition and site data.

Example

The following R packages are required to run the example of this vignette:

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(RESY)

Load the example data

The example data include the species table with the vegetation relevés and the header table with the location of each relevé.

First, load the vegetation relevés:

data_species <- read_csv(
  system.file("extdata", "data_example_species.csv", package = "RESY")
  )
data_species
#> # A tibble: 3,580 × 3
#>    PlotObservationID Cover_Perc scientificName                                  
#>    <chr>                  <dbl> <chr>                                           
#>  1 HU32                     0.1 Dryopteris filix-mas (L.) Schott                
#>  2 HU32                     0.1 Cephalanthera longifolia (L.) Fritsch           
#>  3 HU32                     0.5 Prenanthes purpurea L.                          
#>  4 HU32                     0.5 Anemone nemorosa L.                             
#>  5 HU32                     0.5 Epipactis helleborine (L.) Crantz subsp. helleb…
#>  6 HU32                     0.5 Sorbus aucuparia L. subsp. aucuparia            
#>  7 HU32                    87.5 Fagus sylvatica L.                              
#>  8 HU32                     3   Rubus hirtus Waldst. & Kit.                     
#>  9 HU32                     3   Abies alba Mill.                                
#> 10 HU32                     3   Oxalis acetosella L.                            
#> # ℹ 3,570 more rows

resy_clean_names() removes the author names from the species names and keeps rank markers such as subsp. and var.:

data_species$scientificName <- resy_clean_names(
  data_species$scientificName
  )

Second, load the header table:

data_sites <- read_csv(
   system.file("extdata", "data_example_sites.csv", package = "RESY")
   ) |>
   st_as_sf(coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326)
data_sites

Map the sites

The vegetation relevés of the example dataset are in Tuscany in Italy.

The map shows part of Italy, mainly Tuscany, and the Tyrrhenian Sea. The dots are the locations of the vegetation relevés. Some are on islands.

Get additional data

Load the expert system

resy_load_expert() reads the EUNIS expert system. resy_harmonize_eunis() uses it to check the species names.

parsed_expert_file <- resy_load_expert(scheme = "EUNIS")

Apply resy_harmonize_eunis()

resy_harmonize_eunis() prepares the header table and the species table:

outcome <- resy_harmonize_eunis(
   data = data_sites,
   run_taxonomy = TRUE,
   species_data = data_species,
   parsed = parsed_expert_file,
   run_coast_dunes = TRUE,
   coast_buffer = 5000
   )
#> Warning: "Altitude (m)" is missing. See the "Get altitude data" vignette;
#> altitude rasters are available from mapsforeurope.org.
#> Warning: "Ecoreg" is missing for some plots because they fall outside the
#> ecoregion map.

resy_harmonize_eunis() gives two warnings. The first says that the column Altitude (m) is missing: resy_harmonize_eunis() cannot add it, but vignette("altitude-vignette") shows how to get it. The second says that the ecoregion column (Ecoreg) contains NA values for sites outside the ecoregion base map.

Missing info

These vegetation relevés did not get an ecoregion:

outcome$sites |>
   filter(is.na(Ecoreg))
#> # A tibble: 23 × 11
#>    PlotObservationID Coast_EEA Dunes_Bohn Ecoreg Ecoreg_name Country Country_ID
#>    <chr>             <chr>     <chr>       <dbl> <chr>       <chr>   <chr>     
#>  1 OR48              MED_COAST N_DUNES        NA NA          Italy   IT        
#>  2 EQ56              MED_COAST N_DUNES        NA NA          Italy   IT        
#>  3 IS69              MED_COAST N_DUNES        NA NA          Italy   IT        
#>  4 JP48              MED_COAST N_DUNES        NA NA          Italy   IT        
#>  5 MF17              MED_COAST N_DUNES        NA NA          Italy   IT        
#>  6 SA50              MED_COAST N_DUNES        NA NA          Italy   IT        
#>  7 DR59              MED_COAST N_DUNES        NA NA          Italy   IT        
#>  8 QI21              MED_COAST N_DUNES        NA NA          Italy   IT        
#>  9 PK58              MED_COAST N_DUNES        NA NA          Italy   IT        
#> 10 OY37              MED_COAST N_DUNES        NA NA          Italy   IT        
#> # ℹ 13 more rows
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: Longitude <dbl>, Latitude <dbl>, DEG_LON <dbl>,
#> #   DEG_LAT <dbl>

All 23 of these plots are on the Mediterranean coast (Coast_EEA is MED_COAST), where the ecoregion base map does not reach. Their country was found. In your own data, set their ecoregion before classifying. This example leaves them unset, so resy_classify() evaluates their ecoregion as 0 and warns.

Here is the updated map with the ecoregions in different colors:

Checked species names

outcome$species_checked has one row per species name: the name in the data (scientificName), the name the expert system uses (TaxonName) and whether it matched (matched):

Finalize species data

resy_classify() needs the checked names together with the cover of each species, so the species table is joined to the checked names:

outcome_species <- data_species |>
  left_join(outcome$species_checked, by = "scientificName") |>
  select(PlotObservationID, TaxonName, Cover_Perc)
outcome_species |>
  filter(PlotObservationID == "AE28") |>
  arrange(desc(Cover_Perc), TaxonName)
#> # A tibble: 14 × 3
#>    PlotObservationID TaxonName                 Cover_Perc
#>    <chr>             <chr>                          <dbl>
#>  1 AE28              Mentha requienii                87.5

Classify relevés

resy_classify() classifies the vegetation relevés (obs) using the site data in the header table (header):

res <- resy_classify(
  obs = outcome_species,
  header = outcome$sites,
  scheme = "EUNIS"
  )
#> Warning: `header` is missing columns used by the expert system: Dataset,
#> Altitude (m). Rules using these columns are evaluated with a value of 0.
#> Warning: Header columns used by the expert system have missing values: Ecoreg
#> (23 plots). Conditions on them are evaluated as if the value were 0.
#> Step 5.1  Number of conditions with number of species of a group: 15
#> Step 5.2  Number of conditions with minimum number of species: 127
#> Step 5.3  Number of conditions with sum of square rooted Cover_Perc of species: 140
#> Step 5.4  Number of conditions with total Cover_Perc of the group: 0
#> Step 5.5  Number of conditions with total Cover_Perc of all other species: 1
#>           Number of conditions with total Cover_Perc of all other species except those on the left-hand side: 31
#>           Number of conditions with $05, $25 etc.: 4
#> Step 5.6  Number of conditions with maximum cover of the group: 81
#> Step 5.7  Number of conditions with single species, header levels (e.g. country names): 94
#> Step 5.8  Number of conditions with maximum Cover_Perc in plot: 1
#>           Number of conditions with maximum Cover_Perc in plot EXCEPT species of target group: 0
#> Step 5.9  Number of T$ NON conditions: 140
#> Step 5.10  Header conditions with numeric values: 4
#>   Header conditions with character values: 4
#> adapt conditions 2026-10-29 12:12:41.177606
#> classification from here on 2026-10-29 12:12:41.278297

resy_classify() warns about the site data that is missing: the header has no Altitude (m) and no Dataset column (one EUNIS rule excludes the Swedish National Forest Inventory), and 23 plots have no ecoregion.

Inspect results

Long table of candidates for all plots

Plot AM30 meets the rules of two EUNIS habitat types, T17 and its parent T. It is assigned to T17, which has the higher priority.

cand <- resy_candidates(res, top_n = 3)
cand
#>      plot_id   type priority priority_rank
#>       <char> <char>    <ord>         <int>
#>   1:    AE28      R        1             1
#>   2:    AM30    T17        4             4
#>   3:    AM30      T        3             3
#>   4:    AN57      T        3             3
#>   5:    BE71      T        3             3
#>  ---                                      
#> 301:    ZS46      R        1             1
#> 302:    ZX20    T32        4             4
#> 303:    ZX20      T        3             3
#> 304:    ZX92    T17        4             4
#> 305:    ZX92      T        3             3

wide = TRUE gives one row per plot: the type it is classified as, then its candidate types with their priorities, highest priority first:

resy_candidates(res, top_n = 3, wide = TRUE)
#>      plot_id classification type_1 priority_1 type_2 priority_2 type_3
#>       <char>         <char> <char>      <ord> <char>      <ord> <char>

Plot-level details

resy_eval_plot() prints the full evidence for one plot: its species, which vegetation-type formulas evaluated to TRUE, and the type it is classified as. It then lists the lower-level types the plot did not reach, with the result of each of their conditions, which shows why the classification stopped at this level.

resy_eval_plot(res, p = "AM30") # p = PlotObservationID
#> Types whose rule holds: T17 (priority 4), T (priority 3)
#> Classified as T17 (Fagus forest on non-acid soils), the type with the highest priority.
#> 
#> Plot AM30: 12 species
#>  species                    cover
#>  Fagus sylvatica            87.5 
#>  Prenanthes purpurea         3.0 
#>  Abies alba                  0.5 
#>  Acer pseudoplatanus         0.5 
#>  Athyrium filix-femina       0.5 
#>  Dryopteris filix-mas aggr.  0.5 
#>  Hieracium murorum           0.5 
#>  Solidago virgaurea          0.5 
#>  Sorbus aucuparia            0.5 
#>  Veronica urticifolia        0.5 
#>  Cicerbita muralis           0.1 
#>  Luzula nivea                0.1 
#> 
#> T17 has no lower levels.

Passing type explains any other type in the same way, whether or not its rule holds for the plot:

resy_eval_plot(res, p = "AM30", type = "T17")
#> Types whose rule holds: T17 (priority 4), T (priority 3)
#> Classified as T17 (Fagus forest on non-acid soils), the type with the highest priority.

Print classification hierarchy

resy_expert_tree() prints the type hierarchy of an expert system. In this example, it is the EUNIS expert system, and the tree lists all its types, whether or not they occur in your data. fill = TRUE adds the group levels that the type codes imply but the expert system does not list, here MA2 and MA22. The output is cut to the first 10 types. Descriptions of all EUNIS habitat types are on FloraVeg.EU.

resy_expert_tree(parsed_expert_file, fill = TRUE) |>
  head(10)
#> <resy_expert_tree> 10 node(s), 1 top-level, 2 synthesised group(s)
#> MA Coastal saltmarshes
#>   MA2
#>     MA211 Arctic coastal saltmarsh
#>     MA22
#>       MA221 Atlantic saltmarsh driftline
#>       MA222 Atlantic upper saltmarsh
#>       MA223 Atlantic upper-mid saltmarsh and saline and brackish reed, rush and sedge bed
#>       MA224 Atlantic mid-low saltmarsh
#>       MA225 Atlantic pioneer saltmarsh
#>     MA232 Baltic coastal meadow

References

Chytrý M, Řezníčková M, Novotný P, Holubová D et al. (2024) FloraVeg.EU – an online database of European vegetation, habitats and flora. – Applied Vegetation Science 27, e12798. https://doi.org/10.1111/avsc.12798

Chytrý M, Tichý L, Hennekens SM, Knollová I et al. (2020) EUNIS Habitat Classification: expert system, characteristic species combinations and distribution maps of European habitats. – Applied Vegetation Science 23, 648–675. https://doi.org/10.1111/avsc.12519
